items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The Nazi propaganda chief from 1930 and Reich Minister of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda from March 1933"?
items.answer: Joseph Goebbels
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of Joseph Goebbels.

items.stem: Explain the difference between Nazi propaganda after 1933 and Nazi propaganda before 1933.
items.answer: Before 1933 it competed in elections to win votes; after 1933 it was a state monopoly controlling all media and aimed at mobilisation and consent.
items.markingKey: Before 1933 it competed in elections to win votes; after 1933 it was a state monopoly controlling all media and aimed at mobilisation and consent. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: "Propaganda brainwashed the whole German population into supporting Hitler." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Propaganda reinforced existing beliefs more than it changed minds; the Nazis never won a majority in free elections and many Germans remained unconvinced.
items.markingKey: Propaganda reinforced existing beliefs more than it changed minds; the Nazis never won a majority in free elections and many Germans remained unconvinced. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Source B: Paraphrased from David Welch, British historian, The Third Reich: Politics and Propaganda, 1993

Nazi propaganda was most successful where it built on existing values – nationalism, anti-communism, fear of disorder – and least successful where it tried to change deeply held beliefs, such as religious loyalties.

Explain the view of the use of propaganda in the rise of Hitler and Mussolini that is presented in Source B.
items.answer: Propaganda succeeded mainly by reinforcing existing beliefs rather than converting people.
items.markingKey: Propaganda succeeded mainly by reinforcing existing beliefs rather than converting people. Award 1 mark for each relevant point drawn from the source, up to [2]. Points must come from the source itself; own knowledge is not credited in this question.

items.stem: With reference to the Nazi campaign for the July 1932 Reichstag election, explain how it illustrates the use of modern propaganda methods.
items.answer: The party used posters, films, gramophone records and Hitler’s flights; it became the largest party with 37.3%. It shows how organisation and technology turned economic discontent into votes.

items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against the view that propaganda was the most important reason for Hitler’s rise to power.
items.answer: Propaganda was vital in converting discontent into votes, but Hitler gained power through elite decisions in January 1933.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: Goebbels’ modern campaigns and tailored messages; Hitler myth and rallies; rise from 2.6% to 37.3%. Arguments against: Depression created mass discontent; elite intrigue by Papen and Hindenburg; SA violence and weakness of opponents. Supported judgement: Propaganda was vital in converting discontent into votes, but Hitler gained power through elite decisions in January 1933.

items.stem: Compare and contrast the use of propaganda by two authoritarian leaders in their rise to power.
items.answer: Both used propaganda to build mass followings, though its form reflected each society and the extent to which they also relied on force.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: Hitler: Goebbels, rallies, Hitler myth; Mussolini: Il Popolo d’Italia, myth of action; Mao: Yan’an and rural propaganda; common use of scapegoats and leader image. items.answer: Propaganda worked only where economic and political crisis made people receptive; elite intrigue and violence were also essential.

items.stem: Which king appointed Mussolini prime minister in October 1922?
items.answer: Victor Emmanuel III

items.stem: Distinguish between legal methods and the use of force.
items.answer: Legal methods worked through constitutional channels (appointment, decrees, the Enabling Act, the Acerbo Law); force used SA and squadristi violence and intimidation. Both Hitler and Mussolini combined them in a “legal revolution”.

items.stem: Amara writes: "Hitler seized power in a violent coup in January 1933." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Hitler was appointed chancellor legally by Hindenburg; his earlier coup attempt, the Munich Beer Hall Putsch of 1923, had failed.
items.markingKey: Hitler was appointed chancellor legally by Hindenburg; his earlier coup attempt, the Munich Beer Hall Putsch of 1923, had failed. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Outline one way in which the Matteotti crisis of 1924 shows the combination of force and legality in Mussolini’s rise.
items.answer: After Matteotti denounced Fascist electoral fraud, he was murdered; opposition deputies left parliament (the Aventine Secession) but the king did not dismiss Mussolini. Violence nearly toppled Mussolini, but the legal framework and royal support enabled him to consolidate his dictatorship.

items.stem: Distinguish between Hitler’s rise to power and Mao’s rise to power.
items.answer: Mao came to power through a long revolutionary civil war and peasant mobilisation; Hitler came to power through elections, propaganda and appointment within a constitutional framework.
items.markingKey: Mao came to power through a long revolutionary civil war and peasant mobilisation; Hitler came to power through elections, propaganda and appointment within a constitutional framework. items.answer: It had peasant support through land reform, disciplined forces and effective strategy (e.g. the Huaihai campaign), while the GMD suffered from corruption, hyperinflation, poor morale and military errors.

items.stem: Explain why the leader cult was useful to authoritarian regimes.
items.answer: It created an emotional bond with the population, provided legitimacy beyond the party, allowed the leader to stand above unpopular policies and officials and inspired obedience.

items.answer: Charismatic authority depends on belief in the leader’s extraordinary qualities; legal-rational authority depends on impersonal rules and offices, as in a constitutional state.

items.stem: Evaluate the claim that the weaknesses of the Guomindang were more important than the strengths of the CCP in explaining Mao’s victory in 1949.
items.answer: Both mattered, but the CCP’s ability to exploit GMD weakness through peasant mobilisation was decisive.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: corruption and hyperinflation; loss of urban middle-class support; military blunders in Manchuria. Arguments against: land reform won peasant support; Mao’s guerrilla and mobile strategy; discipline and propaganda. Supported judgement: Both mattered, but the CCP’s ability to exploit GMD weakness through peasant mobilisation was decisive. Markbands: Use the IB Paper 2/3 markbands, scaled to the marks: top band – clearly focused, well structured, accurate and relevant knowledge used to support critical analysis, different perspectives evaluated, reasoned conclusion; middle band – mostly accurate knowledge, some analysis but partly narrative; lower band – little understanding of the demands, mainly description.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "mass rally".
items.answer: A large, carefully staged public meeting used to create a sense of unity and power, such as the Nuremberg rallies
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: a large, carefully staged public meeting used to create a sense of unity and power, such as the Nuremberg rallies. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "squadristi".
items.answer: Fascist armed squads that attacked socialists, trade unions and peasant leagues in 1920–1922
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: Fascist armed squads that attacked socialists, trade unions and peasant leagues in 1920–1922. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Briefly explain why the Long March became important to the CCP despite its heavy losses.
items.answer: It preserved a core of leaders, confirmed Mao’s leadership at Zunyi, spread the party’s message along the route and became a heroic legend of endurance used in propaganda.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: It preserved a core of leaders, confirmed Mao’s leadership at Zunyi, spread the party’s message along the route and became a heroic legend of endurance used in propaganda. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between legal-rational authority and charismatic authority.
items.answer: Charismatic authority depends on belief in the leader’s extraordinary qualities; legal-rational authority depends on impersonal rules and offices, as in a constitutional state.
items.markingKey: Charismatic authority depends on belief in the leader’s extraordinary qualities; legal-rational authority depends on impersonal rules and offices, as in a constitutional state. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Briefly explain why Nazi propaganda was effective in the years 1930–1932.
items.answer: It targeted specific groups (farmers, workers, women) with tailored messages, used modern technology and mass rallies, and offered simple slogans of national unity and scapegoats during the Depression.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: It targeted specific groups (farmers, workers, women) with tailored messages, used modern technology and mass rallies, and offered simple slogans of national unity and scapegoats during the Depression. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between legal methods and the use of force.
items.answer: Legal methods worked through constitutional channels (appointment, decrees, the Enabling Act, the Acerbo Law); force used SA and squadristi violence and intimidation. Both Hitler and Mussolini combined them in a “legal revolution”.
items.markingKey: Legal methods worked through constitutional channels (appointment, decrees, the Enabling Act, the Acerbo Law); force used SA and squadristi violence and intimidation. Both Hitler and Mussolini combined them in a “legal revolution”. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain the difference between Mao’s rise to power and Hitler’s rise to power.
items.answer: Mao came to power through a long revolutionary civil war and peasant mobilisation; Hitler came to power through elections, propaganda and appointment within a constitutional framework.
items.markingKey: Mao came to power through a long revolutionary civil war and peasant mobilisation; Hitler came to power through elections, propaganda and appointment within a constitutional framework. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem:
Source A: Chinese propaganda poster, 1967 (description)

[Poster] A smiling Mao in military uniform stands above a sea of workers, peasants and soldiers waving the Little Red Book; rays of light shine from behind his head. Caption: “Chairman Mao is the red sun in our hearts.”

With reference to its origin, purpose and content, analyse the value and limitations of Source A for an historian studying charismatic leadership and the leader cult.
items.answer: Value: An official poster from the height of the Cultural Revolution, revealing the imagery of the Mao cult. Limitations: It is propaganda showing the image the regime wished to project, not evidence of what people privately believed.
items.markingKey: Value: An official poster from the height of the Cultural Revolution, revealing the imagery of the Mao cult. items.stem: "Mussolini’s propaganda was unimportant because he used only violence." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Mussolini was a former journalist who used Il Popolo d’Italia, rallies and myths of the March on Rome alongside squadrist violence.
items.markingKey: Mussolini was a former journalist who used Il Popolo d’Italia, rallies and myths of the March on Rome alongside squadrist violence. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

How far can Source B be trusted as evidence for the use of force and legal methods in the seizure of power in Germany and Italy? Refer to the origin, purpose and content of the source.

items.stem: A student claims that the CCP won mainly because of Soviet military aid. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Soviet aid (e.g. Japanese weapons captured in Manchuria in 1945) helped, but peasant support, land reform and GMD weakness were more important.
items.markingKey: Soviet aid (e.g. Japanese weapons captured in Manchuria in 1945) helped, but peasant support, land reform and GMD weakness were more important. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Outline one way in which the Nuremberg rallies, especially that filmed by Leni Riefenstahl in “Triumph of the Will” (1935) shows the construction of the leader cult.
items.answer: Riefenstahl filmed the 1934 rally showing Hitler descending from the clouds by plane and reviewing massed ranks. The film presented Hitler as a messianic figure uniting the nation, central to the Hitler myth.
items.markingKey: Context (Riefenstahl filmed the 1934 rally showing Hitler descending from the clouds by plane and reviewing massed ranks.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: The film presented Hitler as a messianic figure uniting the nation, central to the Hitler myth. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the construction of the leader cult.

items.stem: "Propaganda was the most important reason for Hitler’s rise to power." With reference to specific historical evidence, discuss the validity of this view.
items.answer: Propaganda was vital in converting discontent into votes, but Hitler gained power through elite decisions in January 1933.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: Goebbels’ modern campaigns and tailored messages; Hitler myth and rallies; rise from 2.6% to 37.3%; Depression created mass discontent; elite intrigue by Papen and Hindenburg; SA violence and weakness of opponents. items.stem:
Source A: Adolf Hitler, speech to the Reichstag at the Kroll Opera House introducing the Enabling Act, 23 March 1933 (extract, translation)

The government will make use of these powers only insofar as they are essential for carrying out vitally necessary measures. Neither the existence of the Reichstag nor that of the Reichsrat is threatened. The position and rights of the President remain unaffected.

Using the sources and your own knowledge, evaluate the claim that Hitler came to power legally.
items.answer: Hitler’s seizure of power was a pseudo-legal revolution: legal forms disguised the systematic use of force.

items.stem: Evaluate the reasons for the communist victory in the Chinese Civil War (1946–1949).
items.answer: The communist victory resulted from GMD weakness combined with the CCP’s successful mobilisation of peasants.
